title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Lipscomb rituals and recurring events, from painting the campus Bison to student-written mini-musicals and a mascot-led orientation run.

cards.title: Leave a Message on the Bison
cards.subtitle: A reserved painting ritual in Bison Square
cards.notes: Reserve the approved painting period, plan a university-related message and follow the handbook’s content and cleanup rules.
cards.short_summary: Students repaint Lipscomb’s Bison statue to mark university milestones, successes and sponsored events.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb’s 2025–26 student handbook calls painting the Bison statue a time-honored tradition and provides reservation, content and cleanup requirements.
cards.access_notes: The handbook says students must reserve a painting time and comply with university rules governing messages and cleanup.

cards.title: Build a Mini-Musical From Scratch
cards.subtitle: Lipscomb’s three-day student production competition
cards.notes: Watch for the annual category reveal, then see student teams combine original scripts, selected songs, choreography, sets and costumes.
cards.short_summary: Student groups turn one shared category into competing original stage productions.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb documents Singarama as a three-day competition in which student groups write storylines and scripts, select at least eight songs, choreograph, and create sets and costumes.
cards.access_notes: Participation and performance details vary by annual production; consult the university’s current Singarama information before attending.

cards.title: See Tau Phi Stage Its Cowboy Show
cards.subtitle: A social-club country-music production
cards.notes: Check the current production announcement for dates and admission, then expect Tau Phi members to host and perform alongside invited women.
cards.short_summary: A Lipscomb social club carries forward a country-music stage tradition spanning more than four decades.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb identifies the Tau Phi Cowboy Show as a tradition lasting more than 40 years and describes it as a country-music production run, hosted and performed by club members with additional women performers.
cards.access_notes: The university traditions page does not provide a current performance date, admission policy or venue; verify those details before visiting.

cards.title: Turn Dodgeball Into a Costume Matchup
cards.subtitle: An annual themed tournament in Fanning Courtyard
cards.notes: Choose a team theme as well as a roster, then confirm the Student Activities Board’s current Halloween schedule before heading to Fanning Courtyard.
cards.short_summary: Costumed teams transform an annual courtyard dodgeball tournament into a Lipscomb spectacle.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb says its Student Activities Board hosts a themed dodgeball tournament around Halloween each year in Fanning Courtyard.
cards.access_notes: The traditions page establishes the recurring event and location but lists no current date or spectator-access details.

cards.title: Wear Purple and Gold for the Boulevard Battle
cards.subtitle: Lipscomb’s recurring rivalry with nearby Belmont
cards.notes: Confirm the season’s sport, venue and ticket policy, then arrive in Lipscomb colors to join the campus crowd for the crosstown matchup.
cards.short_summary: Two universities on the same Nashville boulevard meet under one rivalry name.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb’s orientation page describes Battle of the Boulevard as a 67-year tradition, while its traditions page identifies Belmont as the rival at the other end of the boulevard.
cards.access_notes: Game dates, host venues and ticket requirements change by season; use the current Lipscomb Athletics schedule before attending.

cards.title: Run Through the Shackleford Road Arch
cards.subtitle: A pep run reborn as a QuestWeek welcome
cards.notes: Follow QuestWeek’s official route and instructions as student-athletes and staff form the cheering finish near the campus entry arch.
cards.short_summary: A former rivalry pep run now welcomes new Bisons during orientation week.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb reports that Running of the Bison began in 2005 and was incorporated into QuestWeek in 2022, with newcomers running through the Shackleford Road entry arch.
cards.source_title: Once a Bison, Always a Bison | Lipscomb University
cards.access_notes: This is an organized QuestWeek activity for new students; participants should follow the current orientation schedule and designated route.

cards.title: Close QuestWeek by Candlelight
cards.subtitle: The ceremony marking new students’ beginning
cards.notes: Check the current QuestWeek program for entry instructions, then attend the candlelight closing ceremony at Collins Alumni Auditorium.
cards.short_summary: New students conclude their first orientation week with a named candlelight ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb’s 2024 back-to-school announcement states that QuestWeek culminates in the candlelight Initium ceremony in Collins Alumni Auditorium.
cards.source_title: Campus comes alive Aug. 12 for the 2024–25 school year | Lipscomb University
cards.access_notes: The documented ceremony is part of QuestWeek; attendance eligibility and timing should be confirmed through current orientation materials.

cards.title: Count Down to the Green’s Holiday Lights
cards.subtitle: Lipscomb’s annual Christmas concert and lighting
cards.notes: Review the annual event page for weather-driven venue changes, arrive before first-come seating fills and stay for the lighting finale.
cards.short_summary: Campus choirs and guest musicians usher in Christmas before Lipscomb lights the green.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb’s event page identifies the 2025 Lighting of the Green as the 21st annual edition and says its concert concludes with the lighting of the green.
cards.source_title: Lighting of the Green | Lipscomb University
cards.access_notes: The 2025 edition moved inside Allen Arena for maintenance; consult the next annual announcement because venue and program details can change.

cards.title: Turn Golf Carts Into Parade Floats
cards.subtitle: A themed student procession during Bisons Weekend
cards.notes: Look up the year’s parade theme and route, then watch student teams translate that prompt into decorated golf-cart entries.
cards.short_summary: Students reinterpret an annual theme by transforming golf carts for the homecoming parade.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb’s history of Bisons Weekend says students decorated golf carts to match selected themes for the student parade in both 2023 and 2024, with another theme set for 2025.
cards.source_title: Once a Bison, Always a Bison | Lipscomb University
cards.access_notes: The route, viewing areas and participation process are set through the current Bisons Weekend program; verify them before visiting.

cards.title: Run the Homecoming 5K for IDEAL
cards.subtitle: A Bisons Weekend race carrying on a 1990s custom
cards.notes: Use the current Bisons Weekend listing to verify registration, route and eligibility before joining or supporting the named annual run.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding homecoming run now appears as Savannah’s Boogie 5K in support of Lipscomb’s IDEAL program.
cards.evidence_claim: Lipscomb states that a 5K became an annual homecoming feature in 1993 and continues as Savannah’s Boogie 5K, an annual event for the university’s IDEAL program.
cards.source_title: Once a Bison, Always a Bison | Lipscomb University
cards.access_notes: Registration requirements, fees and the course are not established on the historical feature; check the current event listing before participating.
